literal: When war has come, a king who has not made defenses, becoming terrified, will swiftly perish.
translation: A king who does not secure his defenses before war arrives will be seized with terror and swiftly perish when the battle comes.
modern: போர் வந்த காலத்தில் தனக்கான அரண் பாதுகாப்பை முன்னரே செய்து கொள்ளாத அரசன், பகைவரைக் கண்டு அஞ்சி, விரைந்து அழிவான்.
explanation: This couplet highlights the critical need for foresight and defensive preparation in statecraft. The word 'ciṟai' refers to fortifications or protective measures. A ruler who fails to build these defenses before a conflict ('ceru') begins will be caught unprepared. When the enemy finally attacks, the ruler will be overcome with sudden panic ('veruvantu') and meet a swift, inevitable ruin ('veytu keṭum').
